summary: Slice 7 (Realtime WSS live tracking) tested end-to-end. Backend: 12/12 pytest pass in /app/backend/tests/test_realtime_ws.py covering all 7 auth-guard branches (missing token → 403, malformed JWT → 403, admin JWT → 403, wrong driver → 403, missing t → 403, wrong share_token → 403, terminal `delivered` job → 403), driver→customer end-to-end broadcast with <1s latency and no duplicates, cross-job isolation (job A publish is NOT delivered to job B customer), throttled Postgres write (5 rapid frames persist only the FIRST coord, a 6th frame 11s later persists again — proving LOCATION_WRITE_MIN_S=10s), server-side ping arrives within 30s of connect, and malformed frame tolerance (lat='oops' ignored, socket stays open, next valid frame fans out). Frontend E2E via Playwright on /send/track/{jobId}?t=...: page renders, `send-track-conn-live` chip visible, driver card shows name/vehicle/plate, customer WS auto-connects to /api/ws/track/{id}?t=..., initial `{type:'hello', driver:{...}}` snapshot received, then a Python-side driver WS client published two location frames (28.61/77.35 → 28.615/77.355) and both were captured on the customer's WebSocket inbound stream within ~500ms. WS routes are additive under new `/api/ws/*` prefix — no impact to existing REST endpoints. Existing GET /api/send/track/{id} REST fallback still returns the safe subset (verified via slice-6 regression test file).
action_items: Non-blocking: Google Maps `DirectionsService` deprecation warning printed on every route refresh (Google is not disabling it, but console noise; plan migration to `google.maps.routes.Route.computeRoutes`).
Non-blocking: Canvas2D getImageData warning (`willReadFrequently`) from Google Maps marker rendering — cosmetic, no user impact.
Consider adding an explicit `/api/admin/drivers/{id}` GET endpoint — the throttled-write test had to use `/api/driver/me` because there's no admin single-driver detail route; admin list is a scan.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py `_persist_driver_location`: fire-and-forget `asyncio.create_task(_persist_driver_location(...))` is invoked on EVERY inbound frame (not just the accepted one) — the throttle-check runs INSIDE the coroutine, so under high frame rate the event loop still schedules N tasks that each open a SessionLocal(). Cheap but not free — consider gating the create_task at the caller site with the same `_last_write_at` check to avoid transient DB pool churn.

routes.py driver WS: `_last_write_at` is a module-level dict keyed only by driver_id, never pruned. Long-running processes accumulate ~200 bytes per unique driver forever. Not urgent (thousands of drivers = kilobytes), but worth a TODO.

routes.py: on driver WS terminal-state reject (`4409 job_terminal`) and role reject (`4401 invalid_token`), the client sees an HTTP 403 during handshake (per Starlette/ASGI). The custom 4401/4403/4409/4404 codes are ONLY visible when the socket was `accept`ed then `close(code=...)`ed — currently the code closes BEFORE accept for all rejects. That means the driver PWA cannot distinguish invalid_token vs not_your_job vs job_terminal on the wire. Consider `await ws.accept()` before `ws.close(code=4xxx, reason=...)` if per-reason UX is desired. (Not tested in E2E — all rejects surface as 403 to Playwright, as expected per Emergent guidance.)

routes.py customer WS `_forward_from_bus`: on `ws.send_json` failure inside the async-for loop, we `return` (goes to finally: stop.set()) but the subscription generator is left iterating. `subscription.close()` in the outer finally handles it, but the `async for` may raise CancelledError inside a `finally: stop.set()` — fine here because stop is idempotent, but a small race window exists where the closing socket sees a new frame just before close. Non-issue in practice.
InProcessPubSub._MAX_LAG=128 with drop-oldest policy is sound for location frames (freshness > completeness). Log a warning when a drop occurs so ops can see slow subscribers. Currently silent.

useJobSocket.js exponential-backoff reconnect (spec'd 1s→20s, reset after 10s stable) — verified indirectly via `send-track-conn-live` visibility, did not exercise the offline-reconnect Playwright path in this run due to time constraints (network-throttling in this MCP env is unreliable). Recommend main-agent self-verify by disabling network in devtools and watching chip flip.

Frontend Playwright: could NOT verify (a) rAF smooth marker interpolation via transform sampling, (b) driver-side outbound throttle (≥2.5s / ≥50m via lastSentRef), (c) Directions refresh policy (<3 req/min) — these require granting geolocation permission + spoofing coords via CDP inside the mcp_browser_automation harness, which supports `context.setGeolocation` only inconsistently. Backend WS delivery + customer inbound path are proven; the driver PWA outbound throttle should be inspected in devtools by main agent.

success_rate.frontend: core P0 flows verified (WS open, hello, live chip, broadcast round-trip); smooth-marker & reconnect P1 flows not exercised — see review comments

context_for_next_testing_agent: Slice 7 backend is fully green (12/12). Regression file /app/backend/tests/test_realtime_ws.py uses `websockets==16.x`; note `InvalidStatus` (not `InvalidStatusCode`) is the exception class in v16 for handshake rejects. All FastAPI WS route rejects (ws.close(code=4xxx) BEFORE ws.accept()) surface to python-websockets as HTTP 403 via `InvalidStatus`, and the assertion pattern is `code in (403, 4xxx)`. When bootstrapping drivers in parallel with pytest-xdist, use distinct `salt` values on the phone generator so no two workers collide. The throttled-write test needs a DEDICATED fresh driver — do not share driver_a because previous tests populate `_last_write_at[driver_id]`. Frontend: mcp_browser_automation cannot reliably simulate the driver PWA's geolocation stream — best pattern is to use Playwright ONLY for the customer /send/track page and drive location frames via a Python websockets client from the same test.
